title: "Isolation movements are useless because you can't really isolate a muscle"
summary: Rebuts the minimalist claim that isolation exercises are useless because true isolation is impossible. Isolation movements prioritise a muscle even if others assist, let you bias regions (e.g. biceps short head) through grip and angle, and allow focused, less taxing work, whereas compounds are a shotgun that let dominant muscles take over. Hypertrophy programs without isolation produce imbalances; don't make a training method your religion.

claims.claim: Many advocates of compounds-only training have glaring imbalances and undeveloped body parts, which shows why isolation matters.
Pure isolation is impossible (curls also involve forearms and shoulders), but that doesn't make a movement useless; it prioritises the target muscle with help from others.
Isolation movements are effectively more precise, focused versions of compound movements, with fewer joints and muscle groups involved.
Compound-only training is a shotgun rather than a sniper: many muscles get worked, but how much each is worked is unknown, which is bad for physique details.
You can't activate only one part of a muscle, but grip and angle shift emphasis, e.g. more short-head and less long-head biceps activation; the same applies to calves and forearms.

Small differences in EMG/activation numbers between exercises (e.g. sumo vs conventional deadlift) don't mean they work the same muscles; the numbers aren't representative, and training with only one or the other yields visibly different development.
In compounds, the dominant muscle takes over and drains the growth from the exercise; isolation lets you put all your effort on one muscle.
Isolation movements are less taxing because you move less weight, so you can slow down and focus on how the movement works the muscle.
Don't let your training regimen become a religion or idolise lifts; use them for results and replace them if they don't deliver.
Running a hypertrophy program with no isolation movements is a big mistake; they're key even for smaller 'show muscles'.
Neglecting isolation can make you strong, but transitioning to aesthetics later means a discouraging uphill battle to catch up neglected muscles.
